speaker: Ange Postecoglou
quote_text:
Yeah, chaotic game for sure. Yeah, we kind of  added to the chaos a little bit. I think some  
of it was self-inflicted, especially in the first  half. Yeah, just with the ball, we were kind of  
really careless with our passing and yeah, that  allowed sort of a game we played on sort of the  
terms Bournemouth would like, you know, with their  transition football. So, yeah, chaotic. Yeah,  
but like I said, 2-0 down, it would have been very  easy to kind of, particularly with the atmosphere  
as it was for the boys to kind of just let the  game get away from us. But yeah, credit to them,  
they found a way to get back in the game and yeah,  we got something out of it. Yeah, that's the key  
thing, they got minutes and you know, I think  Romero, just great to get him back out there,  
he's such an important player for us, but you can  see, you know, he hasn't played for a while. But  
I thought he grew into the game and he got a lot  better as the group went on and great for Djed to  
get 90 minutes in, you know, such a workhorse for  us and I'm sure he'll feel better for that and,  
yeah, brilliant to get Micky out there as well.  So, yeah, I think before Thursday night that was,  
you know, it was key for us to get some minutes  into these guys and thankfully they got through  
it unscathed. Yeah, Lo Celso was great. He's been  great, yeah, but he has played a lot, so again,  
you know, we've just got to be mindful of, you  know, he's becoming an important part of our team,  
and yeah, I thought he made a real big impact when  he came on. He's, like I said, we were just sloppy  
with the ball in the first half, and he's one that  takes a bit more care with it. He's a technician  
and he carries the ball really well, so I thought  he made a real good impact when he came on. As you  
mentioned, he hadn't played for a while. Loose  with his passing to start, we put him in trouble  
a few times. Were you not surprised that he was  a bit rusty after all this time? Well, I mean,  
you're not surprised now. I mean, he hasn't played  for a very long time, and he's hardly played this  
year, to be fair. So, yeah, and you know, Cuti  would be disappointed with that himself, but at  
the same time, what was much more important for me  was how he grew into his game, his defensive work,  
his aerial ability. I mean, he was on the end  of just about every cross we put in the box from  
corners. And defensively, and I think for him,  he'll just feel a lot better having played sort  
of, you know, no, he was only on for forty-five  today, but he was keen to stay on for a bit  
longer, and you can see, like I said, he grew into  the game and really powered for us. How important  
was it to show that spirit, that fight back, and  not lose this game, given where it was at? Yeah,  
look, it was because, you know, you can imagine  sort of the noise around if the players didn't  
respond. And like I said, Thursday night is  obviously a massive game for us and, you know, at  
least from that perspective, and I think even for  the players themselves, you know, we've obviously  
got a challenge on Thursday night, but, you know,  they have become a fairly big challenge today  
and hopefully we show the same sort of mindset.  Fellas, there's a lot of anxiety and that follows  
a play and that's not the case. Yeah, look, again,  I said before, I can't sort of dictate to people,  
you know, how they sort of interact, but,  you know, the crowd certainly helped them  
on Thursday night and, you know, we need our crowd  to get behind the boys on Thursday to make it an  
atmosphere where, yeah, maybe we lose some of  that nervousness and anxiety within our game,  
but the reality of it is, we've, you know, we as  a team have to respond irrespective of whether  
the atmosphere or the other. You know, maybe  if we, you know, if we start the game strong,  
they'll get the… they get the place nice and loud,  which will help us. And Gill, how important was it  
to have that kind of experience on the bench to  change the game in the second half? Yeah, look,  
it certainly helps. It's something we haven't had  for quite a while. And yeah, I thought, you know,  
that all made an impact, you know, particularly Lo  Celso and Sonny when they came on. And you know,  
it was a big moment for Sonny, obviously, taking  the penalty. And you know, he showed for those big  
moments, he's there and an important goal for the  team. And you know, he took that responsibility.  
What did you make of the performance in the  whole? As I said, it was a chaotic game, not a  
lot of control from our perspective, which is not  ideal for the way we want to play. Like I said,  
we looked nervous, we looked anxious, especially  in the first half. But within that context,  
like I said, to come back from 2-0 down, I  think, you know, the positives of that is  
that the lads showed a really strong mindset to  get something out of the game, which, to be fair,  
that's probably what's been missing this year.  I think there's a lot of games we've lost where  
games have just petered out and, you know, if we'd  got sort of more of those single-goal defeats we  
had into draws like we did today, we'd be in  a better position in the league. A lot of your  
games can often be very entertaining, but also  seem quite chaotic. What's the difference between  
a game like that compared to some of those other  fixtures? Is it about control? Yeah, yeah, just, I  
never felt like we sort of had the control or the…  sort of momentum or fluency in the game to be able  
to sort of still make it as kind of high tempo  as possible, but without it having the chaos of  
what it did today, because it ended up becoming a  basketball game and that really suits them. That's  
kind of their template and you need to sort of  control the game more, which we want to do anyway,  
if you want to sort of turn it into a game where  it's high tempo, but less sort of chaotic than  
what it was today. André, because of the injuries  and the sort of schedule, it was a while since the  
team played their usual football, even though  it wasn't perfect. Did you kind of feel with  
the crowd's urgency or was time tight? Look, I  think there was a perseverance there, probably,  
you know, to the angst of our supporters  that they kept trying to play, you know,  
and I think that's important. I think it's the  best way to work your way through the struggle  
we had out there. And like I said, I think you  know, even when sort of Micky came on and you  
saw the drive he has and he's a left-footed sort  of centre-back, you know, it just changes the  
dimensions of how we play. And so there's little  things there that I think certainly, you know,  
from today we'll be able to take into Thursday and  the rest of the season. Mike, last one, please.  
Sorry. No complaints about entertainment, not for  the first time this season, but do you accept that  
on Thursday night you can't afford to be as open  at the back as you were in the first half? Yeah,  
look, I think the openness just came from us  giving the ball away in really key areas. I mean,  
most of the time we were giving the ball away in  pretty critical areas and Vic had to make some  
fantastic saves to sort of keep us in it. So I  don't think it was a case of being open. It wasn't  
like we were, you know, too men forward, it's just  that we're giving the ball away. So we certainly  
need to be better at the way we can execute  that part of our game. Thank you. Thank you.
title: Ange Postecoglou post-match press conference | Tottenham 2-2 Bournemouth
